stories.headline: Harimoto comes back from two games down to win Asian title
stories.summary: Tomokazu Harimoto lost the first two games of the men's singles final in Tashkent to Li Tianyang, then won the next three to take gold. Kuo Guan-hong and Wen Ruibo took bronze.
stories.author: michael

stories.headline: WTT Champions Montpellier draw: Lebrun brothers and Sun Yingsha learn their openers
stories.summary: Félix Lebrun starts against Denmark's Anders Lind on Tuesday evening and Alexis Lebrun meets Germany's Patrick Franziska, while Sun Yingsha's return begins against France's Camille Lutz. Top seeds Sora Matsushima and Wang Manyu face Dang Qiu and Hana Goda.
stories.author: michael
body: The draw for WTT Champions Montpellier pits defending champion Truls Moregard against France's Thibault Poret and Tomokazu Harimoto against Simon Gauzy in the first round. Wen Ruibo and Liang Jingkun meet in an all-Chinese opener, according to Sohu.

In the women's event Miwa Harimoto, who has won the last three Champions titles, plays Bruna Takahashi, Rallys reported. Last year's finalist Sabine Winter faces France's Jia Nan Yuan. Play starts on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Chen Yi sweeps Miwa Harimoto for women's singles gold
stories.summary: China's Chen Yi beat Japan's Miwa Harimoto 3-0 in the women's singles final as China and Japan shared the seven titles between them, four to three.
stories.author: michael
body: China's Chen Yi won the women's singles at the Asian Championships in Tashkent, beating Japan's Miwa Harimoto 3-0 in the final.
Harimoto had a busy week. She lost a second final in the women's doubles, partnering Hina Hayata against China's Kuai Man and Wang Yidi, but won the mixed doubles with Sora Matsushima.
China and Japan shared all seven titles, four to three. Chen Yi is in China's six-strong women's squad for WTT Champions Montpellier, which starts on Tuesday.

stories.headline: China beat Korea for men's team crown; Japan take women's title
stories.summary: China's men won the team final 3-0 against a Korean side that had knocked out world No. 1 Sora Matsushima's Japan in the semi-final. It was Korea's first men's team silver since 2019. Japan won the women's team event.
stories.author: michael

stories.headline: Wang Chuqin pulls out of WTT Champions Montpellier injured as Sun Yingsha returns
stories.summary: Chinese media report that the world champion has withdrawn from WTT Champions Montpellier (27 October to 1 November) with an injury; reports differ on who took his place. Lin Shidong leads China's men and Sun Yingsha heads a six-strong women's squad. Félix and Alexis Lebrun lead the home challenge.
stories.author: michael

stories.headline: Calderano and Diaz win singles titles at Americas Championships
stories.summary: Hugo Calderano beat fellow Brazilian Guilherme Teodoro 4-1 in Lima, and Puerto Rico's Adriana Diaz beat Canada's Mo Zhang 4-2. The USA women won the team event, beating Puerto Rico 3-0 in the final.
stories.author: michael

stories.headline: Pashley and Trumpauskas retain Under-21 National Cup titles
stories.summary: Ella Pashley went unbeaten at Highfields TTC in Wellingborough, beating Sophie Earley 3-0 in the final round. Larry Trumpauskas dropped one match on his way to keeping the men's title.
stories.author: michelle

stories.headline: Sheffield hosts ITTF World Hopes Week
stories.summary: The ITTF's development camp for leading under-12s came to Sheffield. English pair Sai Prasanna Kumar and Isabella Xiao Xu took part, facing playing styles from around the world.
stories.author: michelle
body: Sheffield hosted ITTF World Hopes Week, the federation's development camp for leading young players from around the world.

England's Sai Prasanna Kumar and Isabella Xiao Xu took part. Table Tennis England said the pair faced playing styles they rarely meet at home and learned from the other players and coaches at the camp, and its video report describes the week as a success for players, coaches and the ITTF.

stories.headline: Major League Table Tennis heads to Houston for Week 4
stories.summary: The US franchise league's fourth season continues in Houston from 30 October to 1 November, with four teams in action.
stories.author: michelle
body: Major League Table Tennis continues its fourth season in Houston, with Week 4 running from 30 October to 1 November.
Four of the US franchise league's teams are in action over the weekend, according to Butterfly's preview.

stories.headline: Could a dimpled ball change the game?
stories.summary: Ray D'Alonzo has published a mathematical paper on golf-style dimples on a table tennis ball. His model suggests less drag and more speed retained across the table, though the effects on spin and bounce would need real prototypes to test.
stories.author: tom
body: Ray D'Alonzo has published a mathematical paper asking what would happen if table tennis balls had golf-style dimples.
His model suggests a dimpled ball would meet less drag and keep more of its speed as it crosses the table. He stresses that his drag figures are illustrative rather than measured.
The bigger unknowns are spin and bounce. D'Alonzo concludes that the effect of dimples on either can't be predicted reliably without making and testing real prototypes.

tom.name: Tom Mortimer
tom.bio: Tom Mortimer is a freelance journalist based in Birmingham, writing about sport, politics and where the two meet, with a particular interest in Hungarian football. His work has appeared in The Guardian and The Independent. He started Eleven because table tennis news is scattered across dozens of sites in half a dozen languages.

michael.name: Michael Dobbs
michael.bio: Michael Dobbs is an England-based writer and devoted table tennis fan. With a keen interest in the game, he enjoys following the sport and exploring the stories, personalities and competitions that shape the table tennis world. His writing reflects a genuine passion for the sport and the community that surrounds it.

michelle.name: Michelle Nemeth
michelle.bio: Michelle Nemeth is an England-based writer and passionate table tennis enthusiast. A keen follower of the sport, she combines her love of table tennis with a writer’s interest in the people, stories and developments that make the game so compelling. She brings enthusiasm and a genuine appreciation of the sport to her writing.
